title: ～ことはない — there is no need to ～
summary: Means 'you don't need to ～' and is used to reassure or encourage someone. It follows the dictionary form of a verb.

body.p: 心配することはない, 謝ることはない, 急ぐことはない tell someone who worries too much that it is not necessary. It suits gentle reassurance and encouragement.
～必要はない says objectively that something is unnecessary, while ～ことはない has a caring tone. It is the speaker's advice, not an order. Do not confuse it with ～ことがない (no experience).

examples.ja: 一人（ひとり）で心配（しんぱい）することはないよ。
examples.romaji: Hitori de shinpai suru koto wa nai yo.
examples.tr: There's no need to worry about it alone.

examples.ja: まだ時間（じかん）があるから、そんなに急（いそ）ぐことはない。
examples.romaji: Mada jikan ga aru kara, sonna ni isogu koto wa nai.
examples.tr: There's still time, so there's no need to hurry so much.

examples.ja: あなたのせいじゃないから、謝（あやま）ることはないよ。
examples.romaji: Anata no sei ja nai kara, ayamaru koto wa nai yo.
examples.tr: It isn't your fault, so there's no need to apologize.

pitfalls: Do not confuse ことはない with ことがない, which means 'have never done.'
It is hard to use about yourself; it is basically said about the listener's action.
